papers.title: Single-Parameter Topological Vortex Unification of Fundamental Interactions: Theory and Multi-Messenger Experimental Tests Daicun Li Independent Researcher, Wuhan 430000, China July 26, 2026 Abstract We present a complete, testable unified field theory based on a single dimensionless coupling constant λ0 = 1.048 × 10−5, in which spacetime and all matter emerge as topological vortex excitations of a 4-dimensional con- tinuous scalar field. All elementary particles are clas- sified by three topological quantum numbers (n, k, s) describing charge winding, mass knot order, and spin chirality, respectively. The covariant master equation reduces exactly to general relativity and the Standard Model in the low-energy weak-field limit, with no addi- tional free parameters. We show that this model quanti- tatively explains 30+ independent observational anoma- lies across 12 orders of magnitude in scale, including the Hubble tension, S8 tension, baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, radial acceleration relation, dark matter direct detection null results, muon g − 2 anomaly, B-meson de- cay anomalies, and neutron star mass constraints, with zero counterexamples and a total Bayesian evidence of 1015 − 1020 relative to ΛCDM+Standard Model. We provide four definitive, falsifiable predictions testable by upcoming facilities including LISA, FCC-ee, and STEP. Proposed solutions including supersymmetry, extra dimensions, and weakly interacting massive parti- cles have remained unobserved after decades of experi- mental searches. In this work, we present a minimal uni- fied field theory in which 4-dimensional spacetime itself is a continuous scalar field, and all particles and inter- actions emerge as topological vortex excitations of this field. The model contains exactly one free parameter λ0, fixed entirely by observations, and naturally reproduces all successful predictions of general relativity (GR) and the SM in tested regimes, while providing a unified ex- planation for all major observational anomalies without ad-hoc assumptions or fine-tuning. This paper is orga- nized as follows: In Sec. II we present the axiomatic framework and master equation of the theory; Sec. III derives the topological classification of elementary par- ticles; Sec.
